content:
mina: Uploaded the sigma7b-lite QAT weights to s3://redwood-models/sigma7b-lite/qat/v1/ and pushed a draft model.yaml to the repo. Quick heads-up: tokenizer from upstream has an extra <|pad|> token that shifts ids by +1 compared to our catalog tokenizers.

josh: Thanks — can you paste the model.yaml snippet? Also which checkpoint file name did you use?

mina: Using `sigma7b_qat_2026-03-15.pt` (checked size 13.1GB). model.yaml excerpt:
```yaml
name: sigma7b-lite-qat
version: v1
weights: s3://redwood-models/sigma7b-lite/qat/v1/sigma7b_qat_2026-03-15.pt
tokenizer: huggingface://sigma7b-tokenizer-v2
max_seq_len: 2048
quant: int8
serve_config:
  batch_sizes: [1,4,8,16]
  kv_cache: true
  prefer_fused_attention: false
```

aqi: Noted about the tokenizer mismatch. Upstream tokenizers sometimes add special attrs. Can you diff the vocab? Quick check:
```bash
python -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('vocab.json'))))"
```
If counts differ we need a remap or to vendor the exact tokenizer files. Also runtime: for QAT quant we need the newer fused-attn patch for sequences >512, otherwise p95 blows up.

ravi: Ran a quick perf sweep on a 80GB A100 pool (dev cluster). Results (p50/p95 ms per token generation step, end-to-end generation for 256 tokens):
- batch=1: p50=72ms, p95=98ms
- batch=4: p50=38ms, p95=62ms
- batch=8: p50=28ms, p95=75ms (variance high)
- batch=16: p50=40ms, p95=210ms (regression)

Observation: batch=16 regresses because of padding alignment and suboptimal kernel selection at that occupancy. Also saw a GC spike in our runtime logs at the start of the run.

mina: GC spike is probably from tokenizer init hitting remote HF + cache miss. I can vendor the tokenizer files into the model package and update model.yaml to `tokenizer: file://tokenizer/` — that should avoid cold-start I/O.

leah: For the catalog entry we prefer to have a `perf_notes` field with the exact command you used. Can you paste the run command and env?

ravi: Sure. Command I used:
```bash
export RW_CLUSTER=dev-a100
python infra/perf/run_profile.py --model sigma7b-lite-qat --weights s3://redwood-models/sigma7b-lite/qat/v1/sigma7b_qat_2026-03-15.pt --batch-sizes 1,4,8,16 --seq-len 256 --itrs 30
```
Env: CUDA=12.1, cuDNN=8.8, driver=545.x, rw-runtime=2.8.1-rc.

aqi: Re: kernel selection — I'll run the `kernel_probe` job with `--force-fused-attn true` and report back. If fused fixes p95 at 16 we can add a `serve_hint: prefer_fused_attention: true` in the catalog.

mina: I'll also vendor tokenizer + add a small remap table to handle the extra <|pad|> token (2-3 line script). Will push a PR to `models/sigma7b-lite` and tag @josh for config review.

josh: Pinged. I'll review the model.yaml and the PR tonight. For the GC spike, can you include the runtime logs snippet (stacktrace?) from the start of run? If it's tokenizer I/O we should see `open_file` ops.

ravi: Attached small log excerpt in the PR — shows `cache miss` and a ~1.2s stall at t=0.8s. After warmup steady-state looks fine.

polly-bot: perf-job #2191234 started (sigma7b-lite-qat, batch=16) — tracking at https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/2191234

mina: Thanks all. Action items: 1) mina vendors tokenizer + remap + update model.yaml; 2) aqi runs fused-attn probe and shares perf; 3) josh reviews model.yaml + S3 ACLs; 4) ravi runs extended perfs (seq=1024) once fused-attn patch applied. I'll mark the PR draft and add checklist. :thumbsup:

josh: If everyone agrees, let's block `batch=16` in the catalog until we confirm fused-attn fixes p95. Otherwise list `recommended_batch: 8` in the metadata.

mina: Agreed. I'll add `recommended_batch: 8` and a `notes: avoid batch>=16 on default runtime` line. Will update first_message_ts in the PR body.

leah: Once PR is green, I'll schedule the catalog publish job for the next weekday release.

ravi: I'll re-run overnight with `--seq-len 1024 --itrs 50` and post numbers tomorrow morning.

mina: Cool. Thanks team — ping me if you need the s3 creds (I can grant temporary read-only).

polly-bot: perf-job #2191234 completed: status=running, logs https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/2191234/logs (will update with final metrics).

josh: Sounds good. :eyes:
